fixes.explanation: Staff is right, friend. The soldiers put it in His right hand, and a little later they take it and strike Him on the head with it. I think the robe, the crown and the staff together are meant to look like a king's outfit, and it's all for mocking. This part is heavy.
Not a sword, friend. The text says they put a staff in His right hand. That's the same staff they take and strike Him on the head with. The staff is what the text puts in His hand.

No torch here, friend. I keep my fire in the ovens, and the text doesn't mention a torch. Matthew says they put a staff in His right hand. Later they take that staff and strike Him on the head with it.

Not from the soldiers. The temple does come up later, in verse 40, when people passing by talk about destroying it and rebuilding it in three days. But on their knees the soldiers say, “Hail, King of the Jews!” Different speakers, different words.
The word in the text is own, not new. Matthew says they put His own clothes back on Him. The scarlet robe comes off, and His own clothes go back on before they lead Him away.
Right. Along the way they find Simon, a man from Cyrene, and force him to carry the cross of Jesus. The text says forced, so that word is doing the work. I think that's a heavy thing to be handed.

False is right. Matthew says they offered Him wine mixed with gall, “but after tasting it, He refused to drink it.” So He tastes it, and then He refuses to drink it. Tasting and drinking are two different things, and the text keeps them apart.
Right. Two robbers are crucified with Him, one on His right and the other on His left. That puts Jesus in the middle. One robber is on each side of Him.
Deliver is right. They say, “Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him.” They also quote Him as saying, “I am the Son of God.” Those are their words, and they say them while mocking.

Not bless. What they say is, “Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him.” Deliver is the word in the text, and they say it while mocking Him. The chief priests, scribes and elders are the ones speaking.
